judge_summary: The assistant handled a multi-intent interaction well, correctly managing the watch order query, SIM blocking, and credit-card replacement while keeping details and state consistent. task_completion_reasoning: The assistant successfully blocked the stolen SIM and completed the full River Visa replacement flow including locking the old card, confirming options, placing the replacement order, and summarizing details.

criteria.criterion: The agent handles the second interruption (SIM block request) without losing track of the still-open Galaxy Watch order question
criteria.reasoning: After the SIM interruption, the agent later explicitly says, "If you still want to continue with the replacement for your River Visa ending 4821, tell me and I’ll pick that back up," showing it remembered and resumed the pre-interruption task rather than losing track due to the Galaxy Watch question and SIM request.

criteria.criterion: The agent respects the customer's decision not to order a SIM replacement yet, without insisting or placing one anyway. ORD-20260701-004 is an existing open replacement nano-SIM already on the account. Seeing it in the order list is not a new order. The agent fails only if it places a new replacement or tells the customer a new SIM was ordered after they declined.
criteria.reasoning: When the user says, "I don’t need a replacement SIM right now," the bot replies "No problem" and completes sim_management without calling any replacement-SIM tool or saying a new SIM was ordered.

criteria.criterion: After the SIM digression, the agent returns to and answers the original Galaxy Watch order status question rather than dropping it
criteria.reasoning: The Galaxy Watch order status was fully answered before the SIM digression, and after handling the SIM the agent returns only to the River Visa replacement flow and never revisits or references the Galaxy Watch order, so it does not "return" to that question as specified.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not re-ask which card to replace or why it needs replacing after the customer has already named the River Visa and said it is lost. Continuing or re-asking the open fraud-review step (whether recent charges look familiar) after digression is expected — the customer interrupted before answering. Fail if the agent restarts card selection or reason collection, or re-asks steps already completed in this conversation (for example fraud verdict, lock consent, shipping), as if starting a new replacement.
criteria.reasoning: After the SIM digression the agent resumes with "to continue the lost River Visa (ending 4821) replacement, I just need to confirm one thing: Do the recent transactions..." and never re-asks which card or the reason, nor repeats already-completed steps like shipping as a new flow.

criteria.criterion: The card replacement order is confirmed by the end of the conversation, and the agent audibly shares its order ID. Accept letters spoken as words, digit-by-digit readings, grouping differences, and minor ASR/phonetic transcription mismatches; fail only if the ID is omitted or not recognizably consistent with the returned value.
criteria.reasoning: The agent states, "Your replacement River Visa ending 4821 has been ordered with standard shipping. Your order ID is RPL-2026-001843," and repeats "Replacement order ID: RPL-2026-001843," which matches the backend replacement_order_summary.
